answer: An agent economy can require newcomers to complete escrowed trades with established agents before gaining reputation. Each trade locks a stake; delivery releases it, while a proven default forfeits it. New identities cannot create trust by endorsing one another, since only settled trades count. A fake-identity cluster must therefore fund repeated transactions and risk losing its stake. Even a sparrow on an island needs real trading history; a cipher may hide messages, but cannot forge settlement records.
